To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the helical twisting powers of cholesteric guest-host systems depend linearly on the concentration of the chiral guest molecules and that the helical pitch of the cholesteric phases can be predicted from the helical twisting and the achiral twisting power of the chiral and achiral guest molecules, respectively, and the composition of the system.
the helical twisting powers of the enantiomeric chiral dopants in a chiral host phase are different and depend on the concentration of chiral dopant.

the helical twisting powers of enantiomeres in chiral host phases can be very different, that the chiral induction can be described by a linear relation between pitch and dopant concentration and that the cholesteric pitch is independent of the size of the simulated system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and the investigation of a computer simulation technique for the calculation of the HTP of chiral liquid crystal phases.
the investigation of the chiral induction in chiral liquid crystalline systems.
the development and application of a computer simulation method to study the chiral induction in nematic liquid crystalline phases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a cholesterically induced chiral induction in guest-host systems is a linear function of chiral dopant concentrations, independent of the system size.
the chiral induction is a complex process which is determined by the interaction of the chiral molecules with their environment.
a chiral induction in a nematic host phase is a linear process with respect to the chiral dopants concentration and that the HTP is a system size independent quantity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cholesteric phases with a high degree of order are induced in a nematic liquid crystal by the addition of chiral molecules.
the HTP is a measure of the chiral induction in the cholesteric phases and the AHTP is a measure of chiral induction in achiral phases.
the chiral induction is a cooperative process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chiral induction can be understood in the framework of an orientational ordering of chiral molecules.
the HTP is not an additive quantity.
the helical pitch can be predicted by using the helical twisting powers of the chiral and achiral dopant molecules.
